target.name: Radify Metals
target.founder: Zach Detweiler, Dan Bullard, Bryce Parrish, Zach Murphree

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Radify Metals operates in Robotics & Manufacturing at an undisclosed stage, attempting valuation against a universe of 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow peer clustering. Of 11 same-sector peers identified in Robotics & Manufacturing, zero met simultaneous stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier criteria. The analysis required a minimum of 3 datapoints within filtered categories to produce a defensible median; this threshold was not met. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material comparability risk and was rejected on methodological grounds.

The absence of tight-filter comparables reflects either genuine differentiation within Radify's subsector positioning or sparse data availability at the target's stage. Without triangulation across trading multiples, precedent transactions, or DCF anchoring to disclosed financials, a quantitative range cannot be supported from the provided dataset. Valuation work on this target should prioritize obtaining detailed financials from Radify and recent round terms from the peer set to enable either a revised peer-median approach or alternative methods such as transaction-based analysis. Key uncertainties include the company's actual stage, revenue scale, and capital efficiency relative to the identified competitor set.
